feeds.title: Multiple Sclerosis News Today
feeds.description: Stay informed about approved therapies, new medications and developments to treat MS. Hear patient and caregiver voices from one of the largest MS communities online. Multiple Sclerosis News Today is a digital news publication dedicated to offering comprehensive daily news coverage of MS.

feeds.title: The MS-Blog
feeds.description: A blog for people with MS and their families, by Barts and The London School of Medicine and Dentistry.

feeds.title: Multiple Sclerosis Association of America Blog
feeds.description: The Multiple Sclerosis Association of America (MSAA) is a national nonprofit organization dedicated to enriching the quality of life for everyone affected by multiple sclerosis. MSAA provides ongoing support and direct services to individuals with MS, their families, and their care partners.

feeds.title: Life in Spite of MS Blog
feeds.description: Life in Spite of MS seeks to provide information, support, and inspiration to anyone who suffers from multiple sclerosis. Information and tips for family members and caregivers is also provided.

feeds.title: Fightmsdaily
feeds.description: Living life with a chronic illness is definitely not easy. But I do my best to push through all the barriers this illness puts in front of me! In my heart and mind, I believe maintaining a positive outlook on all situations in life will carry us through to much better times! I hope you find the information that I provide both helpful and inspirational!

feeds.title: Fundación GAEM | Multiple Sclerosis Sufferers
feeds.description: We are the first and only non-profit private patients foundation to boost biomedical innovation.Located at the Scientific Park of Barcelona and under the direction of research and biomedicine experts. We select innovative projects that can become therapeutical solutions for healing Multiple Sclerosis and for improving the quality of life of MS sufferers.

feeds.title: Life on a Seesaw
feeds.description: Kat Naish created Life on a Seesaw blog as a place to share her journey as a working mummy and dealing with a recent diagnosis of multiple sclerosis.

feeds.title: A Couple Takes on MS
feeds.description: Dan & Jennifer Digmann writes about experiences, insights, and perspectives on pushing through the constant challenges and storms of daily life with and without multiple sclerosis.

feeds.title: Tripping on Air Blog
feeds.description: Life hacks from a girl with MS. How to trip and fall without wrecking the pretty.

feeds.title: Dinosaurs Donkeys and MS Blog
feeds.description: I'm Heather, a 27 year old actor, teacher and MS Society Support Volunteer, who lives in England and was diagnosed with MS 2 years ago. Blogging about Life with MS.

feeds.title: Ireland Multiple Sclerosis & Me
feeds.description: Ireland, Multiple Sclerosis & Me is about conveying optimism and motivation through writing about ​life with MS, while also sharing facts, figures and trends and the mission is to enable and empower people affected by Multiple Sclerosis to live the life of their choice to their fullest potential.

feeds.title: Yvonne deSousa.com Blog
feeds.description: The goal of www.yvonnedesousa.com is to help people struggling with illness or any unfunny thing to have a little smile. If anyone viewing the website laughs out loud, even better. To do this, I poke gentle fun at myself, MS and the world around me.

feeds.title: Bethy Bright and Dark
feeds.description: I'm Beth Nigro, 50 years old, single and I live happily with my four cats Fred, Ivan, Owen and Roger. I was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2015 after a three year journey of mysterious ills and bodily failings that left me feeling confused, frustrated and just plain pissed off. I blog about my life with multiple sclerosis - and my life in general.

feeds.title: Enjoying the Ride
feeds.description: Welcome to my blog. I've started this blog to help me pass the time while engaged in a productive activity- advocating for the disabled community, of which I am now a reluctant member. I am Mitch, and despite everything I am still Enjoying the Ride.

feeds.title: My Self-healing Journey
feeds.description: This is a blog about Multiple Sclerosis and healing. Learn about how I was diagnosed and my ups and downs while I traverse through life. I hope that you find inspiration, love and hope as you read about our ups and downs and my current journey of wellness through the mind-body connection.

feeds.title: Multiple Sclerosis Society of Canada Blog
feeds.description: The Multiple Sclerosis Society of Canada is the source of accurate, up-to-date information about MS, the most common neurological disease affecting young adults in Canada. We are a leader in finding a cure for multiple sclerosis & enhancing the quality of life for those affected.

feeds.title: A 30 Minute Life
feeds.description: My Blog about Multiple Sclerosis and Chronic Headache. Imagine a life that can only be lived 30 minutes at a time. This blog will reflect my thoughts, and musings, about this lifestyle.

feeds.title: Tripping Through Treacle
feeds.description: Want to know what life is like with Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis? Read on! In my personal lifestyle blog, I share my daily trials and tribulations and my current treatment using HSCT. I am a 'spoonie' parent and try to live as healthily as I can with a chronic, progressive disease.

feeds.title: it's only a bruise.
feeds.description: I started this blog to help facilitate conversations about multiple sclerosis between myself and my friends, after being diagnosed with RRMS in 2013. The disease makes people - myself included - uncomfortable. The internet can be a scary place, particularly during diagnosis and in the months following. So stick around to read my thoughts on health, wellness and advocacy.

feeds.title: think in decimals
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Edith Solenne Monk. I was diagnosed with MS at 16, and as much as I hate that being my opening line, it's become a big part of my life. In 2012 I moved on to Tysabri (natalizumab) infusions every four weeks, but the disease progression didn't slow. Following a nasty UTI in 2013, I became reliant on crutches to walk. Today, I'd say I'm used to being disabled, but with the challenges of MS constantly shifting, and my 30s bringing in a new chapter, there's still plenty to talk about.

feeds.title: It's a Shit Business
feeds.description: It's a Shit Business is a blog by Steve Domino where he shares about his life with Multiple Sclerosis and writes light-hearted jokes.

feeds.title: M.S. Views & News.
feeds.description: A web-blog (formerly known as Stu's Views and MS News), now published by MS Views and News, a patient advocacy organization. The information on this blog helps to Empower those affected by Multiple Sclerosis globally, with education, information, news and community resources.

feeds.title: Girl with MS
feeds.description: Caroline Craven is an Award-winning Blogger, Speaker who is living with Multiple Sclerosis. In my blog you will know about my experiences and how to live better with MS & chronic illness.

feeds.title: My New Normals
feeds.description: My New Normals was created to give an outlet to family, friends, caregivers and anyone living with MS or any other debilitating disease. Our goals are to raise national awareness and educate the public about MS.

feeds.title: Dan and Jennifer Digmann Blog
feeds.description: Dan and Jennifer demonstrate two different faces of Multiple Sclerosis. We are using our experiences to empower others.

feeds.title: My Odd Sock
feeds.description: My Odd Sock is my glimmer of inspiration, a creative dream of a lifetime! A funny guy with multiple sclerosis. MS confirmed by MRI. Funny still up for debate.

feeds.title: THRIVING BEYOND DISABILITY
feeds.description: My name is Denise Rogers. I became disabled after having 6 surgeries on my Thoracic Spine from T2-T9. This blog is about getting my life back. It is about learning to live with chronic pain as well as being disabled, dealing with depression, regaining confidence and control ,learning to feel beautiful again, and all the while navigating medications, treatments and life. Lots of prayer, family, and God help me get through it.

feeds.title: Ashley's Life with Multiple Sclerosis
feeds.description: I'm a blogger for MultipleSclerosis.net and an MS Patient advocate. I've had my ups and downs in living this new journey with MS and I like to express my MS by supporting and helping educate others, as well as blogging. Hoping that others can relate and find help/reassurance with my MS advocacy & blogging!

feeds.title: Dave's ActiveMSers Blog
feeds.description: This is the official blog of ActiveMSers, which is designed to help, motivate, and inspire those with multiple sclerosis to stay as active as possible—physically, intellectually, and socially—regardless of physical limitations. Our motto: Be active, stay fit and keep exploring!

feeds.title: Society for Multiple Sclerosis Patients in Pakistan Blog
feeds.description: The Society for Multiple Sclerosis Patients in Pakistan is aimed at creating awareness about MS among the general population and helping MS patients cope with this disease.

feeds.title: One Man and His Catheters
feeds.description: I aim to be (mostly) positive, witty (when I can be!), and raw (because I try to help people understand life with Multiple Sclerosis and disability. 'A good life (honestly!) with Multiple Sclerosis... I work (for now), I love, I live, I have fun. Just with wheelchairs and drugs and spasms and stuff...'

feeds.title: MSsymptoms.me
feeds.description: MSsymptoms.me is a resource for patients, family, and friends of people with multiple sclerosis. In this blog. author Melissa Cook discusses the ways MS has affected my life and the latest research.

feeds.title: Multiple experience
feeds.description: My blog will always have some spiritual tones to it because I believe in what I am doing, but I am not a preacher. I am a happier person today because I'm happier with myself. I'm able to not only finally recognize, but be grateful for the abundance of love around me. This blog is about life, being single, being a parent, challenges of symptoms, good days, bad days and all the days in between.

feeds.title: Accessible Rach
feeds.description: I am a 50 plus Yorkshire disabled blogger who following a diagnosis of Primary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis turned to writing as an outlet. I write insightful articles that highlight accessibility at events, mainly Rugby League events at present. I travel to different grounds to complete accessibility assessments, noting their good features and what can be improved.

feeds.title: BBH with MS Blog
feeds.description: I am Megan living With Multiple Sclerosis and Finding The Reasons to Laugh and Smile. I hope you will be able to say you do, once you have read about how I view all the ups and downs that life seems to deal each and every one of us. There is the good, the bad and the ugly….and then there are the reasons to laugh and smile.

feeds.title: Love My MS Life
feeds.description: My name is Tricia, and I live in San Diego. My goal is to inspire you. I share bits and pieces of my life and experiences living with MS with the goal of giving you the one thing that keeps me going every day: hope.

feeds.title: MultipleSclerosis.net
feeds.description: At MultipleSclerosis.net we empower patients and caregivers to take control of MS by providing a platform to learn, educate, and connect with peers and healthcare professionals.
